body:
# Ledger: expense, income and transfer entries — design of record

Decided with the maintainer on 2026-09-20. Expense lists become **ledgers**. Every entry is
exactly one of three types. This document is the contract the server, the web client and the
Android client all implement; when it and the code disagree, the code is wrong.

## 1. Entry types and their arithmetic

An entry keeps today's shape: `paid_by` (map account -> amount) and `paid_for` (map account ->
amount), both non-empty, both summing to the same total T, `equal_by`, `equal_for`, `date`. Every
amount stays a POSITIVE decimal string; nothing negative ever goes on the wire. A new key
`type` says what the entry is. The sign lives in the type, not in the amounts, so that an entry
is "exactly one of the three" structurally.

| type | meaning | net spent | effect on the balance of account a |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expense` | someone paid for the group (today's behaviour) | +T | `paid_by[a] - paid_for[a]` |
| `income`  | the group received money (refund, deposit, sale) | -T | `-(paid_by[a] - paid_for[a])` |
| `transfer`| one member pays another directly (settlement) | 0 | `paid_by[a] - paid_for[a]` |

For `income`, `paid_by` reads "received by" and `paid_for` reads "credited to". For `transfer`,
`paid_by` is the single sender and `paid_for` the single recipient.

### Per-participant figures (both clients, identical)

For each account a, over all entries:

* expense: `paid += paid_by[a]`, `share += paid_for[a]`
* income:  `paid -= paid_by[a]`, `share -= paid_for[a]`
* transfer: `settled += paid_by[a]`, `settled -= paid_for[a]`   (sent minus received)

`balance = paid - share + settled`. Transfers are deliberately kept OUT of paid/share, so those
two stay "what this person spent / consumed" and a settlement never inflates them; `settled`
carries the transfers so that the three figures always add up to the balance.

Invariant (must be a property test on both clients): the balances of all participants sum to
zero, for any mix of the three types. `settle()` (who pays whom) is unchanged and takes balances.

### Net spent

`expensesCents` = sum of T over expense entries; `incomeCents` = sum of T over income entries;
`netCents = expensesCents - incomeCents` (may be negative). Transfers count for nothing.
"Total spent" becomes **"Net spent"** everywhere (list header, Balances page, Overview card) and
is shown in the neutral text colour, never red/green.

### Effect of one entry on one account

`entryEffectCents(entry, account)` = the row of the table above, in cents (signed). Shown on
entry rows (section 5). Zero (or not involved) shows nothing.

## 2. Wire format

```json
"expense": {"value": {
  "type": "income",
  "paid_by": {"<account>": "30.00"}, "equal_by": true,
  "paid_for": {"<a>": "10.00", "<b>": "10.00", "<c>": "10.00"}, "equal_for": true,
  "date": "2026-09-17"
}}
```

* The list `kind` stays `"expenses"` and the item field stays `expense`. Only display strings
  change to "Ledger" / "entry". (Renaming the wire would break stale clients for no user benefit.)
* `type` is one of `"expense"`, `"income"`, `"transfer"`. Absent means `"expense"` (all data
  written before this change). Any other value, or an explicit null, is `422 invalid_expense`.
* The server stores `type` normalised (always present after a write) and, when serving a row
  written before this change, adds `"type": "expense"` on the way out, so a reader always sees
  it. Clients still default an absent `type` to `expense` defensively.
* Transfer shape: `paid_by` has exactly one entry, `paid_for` has exactly one entry, the two
  account ids differ, the amounts are equal (already implied by the equal-sum rule), and
  `equal_by` and `equal_for` are booleans as always (clients send true).
* Everything else is unchanged: positive amounts only, at most 200 participants per map, both
  maps sum to the same cents, participants are current members or already in the stored entry,
  the date rules, unknown keys dropped. These shape rules are context-free and apply to every
  write; the membership rule still applies only to a write that would win last-write-wins.
* This is a protocol change (see the protocol-versioning spec): PROTOCOL_VERSION becomes 3.

### The freeze (closing rule) becomes type-aware

`closing.expense_amounts` must apply the type's sign (income negated; transfer like expense),
so a write that changes what a frozen participant paid or owes is still `participant_frozen`.
In addition: a write that changes an entry's **type** counts as changing every account involved
in it. So flipping an entry between expense and transfer (same amounts, different type) is
`participant_frozen` when any involved account is frozen (has voted, or is no longer a member),
and allowed otherwise. Creating or deleting an income or transfer follows the existing
"from zero" / "to zero" rule.

## 3. The entry dialog (web and Android identical in behaviour and wording)

* A segmented control at the top: **Expense | Income | Transfer**. New entry defaults to
  Expense. Editing an existing entry shows its type and allows changing it (that is also how an
  old "Settlement" recorded as an expense gets corrected).
* Title, date, note, total: as today for all three types.
* Expense: exactly today's form and labels. Income: same form, labels "Received by" (payers
  section) and "Credited to" (beneficiaries section). Transfer: no split UI; two single-choice
  pickers **From** and **To** (members; each excludes the other's choice) plus the total.
* Switching type keeps title, date, note and total. Expense <-> Income keeps the participant
  maps. Switching TO Transfer: if the maps are not already one sender and one recipient, reset
  to From = me (or the first payer), To = the first other member (or the first beneficiary that
  differs from From). Switching FROM Transfer: the sender becomes the sole payer/receiver, the
  recipient the sole beneficiary, equal split of one each.
* Validation messages exist for: transfer sender equal to recipient, transfer needing two
  different members (a list with one member cannot record a transfer: disable that segment).
* A blank title is refused for an expense as today; for Income and Transfer it defaults to the
  type's localized label ("Income", "Transfer"). The Balances "Reimburse" action pre-fills the
  existing localized "Settlement" title and type Transfer, From = debtor, To = creditor.
* Existing rules stay: frozen participants cannot be selected/changed, voters cannot edit, a
  closed list is read-only, delete works as today.

## 4. Names and wording

* The list kind is called **Ledger** (display only). Its description (the one under the kind
  radio in "New list"): "Shared money: who paid, who received, who owes what."
* The two tabs of a ledger are **Entries | Balances** (was Expenses | Balances).
* "Add expense" becomes **"Add entry"**. Wherever the UI says "expense" for something that can
  now be any of the three types, say "entry"; keep "expense" only where the type Expense is
  meant. Reuse each locale's existing vocabulary for "expense" as the Expense type label, and
  add Income and Transfer beside it.
* Suggested translations for the kind name (agents may adjust with a reason): de Kassenbuch,
  fr Livre de comptes, es Libro de cuentas, pt-BR Livro-caixa, uk Книга обліку, ar دفتر
  الحسابات, ja 帳簿, zh-Hans 账本. Type labels: de Ausgabe/Einnahme/Überweisung,
  fr Dépense/Revenu/Virement, es Gasto/Ingreso/Transferencia, pt-BR Despesa/Receita/
  Transferência, uk Витрата/Надходження/Переказ, ar مصروف/دخل/تحويل, ja 支出/収入/振替,
  zh-Hans 支出/收入/转账.

## 5. Screens

* **Entry rows** (list of entries, newest date first as today): title, and for income and
  transfer a small muted type badge (text: "Income" / "Transfer") next to it; sub-line: expense
  "Paid by A · for B, C" (existing string), income "Received by A · for B, C", transfer
  "A → B" (existing "{from} → {to}" string). Right side: the entry total in the NEUTRAL text
  colour (income prefixed "+"), and under it, small, **my effect** as a signed amount in the
  balance colours (green when > 0, red when < 0, "+" prefix on positives; nothing when 0 or I am
  not involved).
* **List header**: "Net spent" (neutral) and "Your balance" (coloured, signed) as today.
* **Balances page**: "Net spent" strong; when income exists a muted line "Expenses {spent} ·
  Income {income}". Per person: first line name and the coloured signed balance; second line
  "Paid {paid} · Share {share}" and, when settled is not zero, " · Settled {settled}" (signed,
  uncoloured). Settle-up section unchanged apart from Reimburse creating a Transfer.
* **Overview card**: the list total is net spent; the balance stays coloured.
* Colours: only a person's own position is coloured (red owe, green owed, grey square);
  entry amounts and totals never are. The balance-colour tokens come from the colours ticket.

## 6. Shared test cases (shared-test-cases/expense-arithmetic.json)

The file keeps its name. Extend it, then both implementations pass it:

* every `balances` case gets expected `settled` (as "0.00" where none); expenses in cases may
  carry `type` (absent = expense);
* new cases: income alone; the refund scenario (hand-verified, use it verbatim): A pays 60
  for A,B,C (20 each) as an expense; B pays A 20 as a transfer; A receives a 30 refund credited
  to A,B,C (10 each) as income -> A paid 30, share 10, settled -20, balance 0; B paid 0,
  share 10, settled 20, balance 10; C paid 0, share 10, settled 0, balance -10; net spent 30
  (expenses 60, income 30); a transfer that settles a debt exactly to zero; a transfer between
  two people who are not debtors; income larger than expenses (negative net); uneven income
  split (10.00 over three: leftover cents go to the first participants as for expenses); a
  mixed ledger with all three types and more than two participants;
* new group `spent`: entries with types -> expected `{expenses, income, net}`;
* new group `effect`: entry + account -> expected signed effect ("0.00" where not involved);
* `settle` cases keep working unchanged.

Both clients additionally carry a seeded property test: random ledgers of all three types over
2-5 participants; assert that balances sum to zero, that settling the suggested transfers
brings every balance to zero, and that net = expenses - income.
title: Ledger: expense lists become ledgers with expense, income and transfer entries (design)
